_note: Informe de fin de partida. recap_fragments: frases según banderas, en orden de prioridad (se muestran hasta 3, salteando las de recap_skip del final). lenses: textos de los tres modelos de Allison.
goal_line: October 1962 could have ended ten different ways. Find them all.

recap_fragments.text: One of your orders arrived too late.
Some squadrons never heard the recall.
You let the military retaliate without asking you.
You raised the alert to DEFCON 2.
You answered the U-2 shootdown with force.
You held back after the U-2 was shot down.
You held the line in Berlin.
You made a promise about Turkey that could never be public.
You traded the Jupiters in public.
You promised not to invade Cuba.
You opened a back channel to Moscow.
You widened the room, and the secret leaked.

rational.name: Rational Actor
rational.line: You compared the options and picked the one that served your goal.
rational.dominant: You played this crisis mostly as a calculation: what do I want, what does each option cost, which one gets me there. It is how most people imagine a president deciding.

organizational.name: Organizational Behavior
organizational.line: You chose between plans the Navy, the Air Force or the CIA had already written.
organizational.dominant: Most of your crisis was shaped by what the military and the agencies were already prepared to do. You picked between their plans, and they carried them out their way.

governmental.name: Governmental Politics
governmental.line: The decision came out of an argument between your advisers.
governmental.dominant: Most of your crisis was settled by argument: who was in the room, who leaked, whose advice you took. The decision came out of that struggle.

timeout_line: %d of your decisions were made by the clock: the organization did what it was already going to do.
lenses_intro: Political scientist Graham Allison asked why governments decide what they decide. He found three different kinds of answer. Each decision you made fits one of them best. These are not scores.
lenses_tie: Your crisis was split between the three. That is Allison's point: you need all three to explain what happened in 1962.
lenses_note: None of them is the right way to play. Allison's argument is that each one explains part of what happened and misses the rest.
